In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
 Cra No. 11774 of 2025
 (Thakur @ Thakriya And Others Vs The State Of Madhy
 Dated : 01-04-2026

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Mohit Pandya - Advocate for the appellant.
Ms. Usha Chouhan - G.A. for the respondent/State.

Heard on I.As. No.4207/2026 - for appellant No.1 Thakur @ Thakriya and 1628/2026 - for appellant No.2 Kalusingh , which are applications under Section 430 of BNSS, 2023 for grant of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence on behalf of the appellants.

2. Appellants have been convicted under sections 420/120(B), 419 (3 counts)/120(B), 467 (03 counts)/120(B), 468 (03 counts)/120(B) and 471 (03 counts)/120(B) of the IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 7 years with fine of Rs.1,000/-, R.I. for 3 years with fine of Rs.3,000/-, R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.6,000/-, R.I. for 7 years with fine of Rs.3,000/- and R.I. for 3 years with fine of Rs.3,000/- for each appellant with usual default stipulations vide order dated 10.11.2025 by Second Additional Sessions Judge, Manawar, Dhar in ST No.49/2022 in connection with Crime No.142/2022.
3.

entities.text: Second Additional Sessions Judge, Manawar, Dhar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellants has submitted that the appellants are innocent and they have falsely been implicated in the present case.
The appellants have suffered almost four years of detention and there is no possibility of hearing of the appeal in near future.
The appellants are ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by the Court.
Therefore, if the jail sentence is not 2 CRA-11774-2025 suspended, the purpose of filing this appeal would become futile.
4. Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the application for suspension of sentence.

5. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the appellants have suffered almost 4 years of their jail sentence and final hearing of the appeal will take sufficient long time for its disposal, without commenting on the merits of the case, the applications are allowed and it is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if already not deposited, the appellant No.1 - Thakur @ Thakriya and appellant No.2 - Kalusingh shall be released on bail, on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) each with a separate solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of Trial Court, for their appearance before the Registry of this Court firstly on 04.08.2026 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this Thakur @ Thakriya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46601584/
1 regard, till final disposal of this appeal.
6.

entities.text: Thakur @ Thakriya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of above, I.As.No.4207/2026 and 1628/2026 stand disposed of.

7. List for final hearing in due course.
(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE Vatan Thakur @ Thakriya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46601584/
